candidates.exact_span: Revised TDS net incremental increase limit and mass loading limit have been established;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes that revised TDS incremental-increase and mass-loading numeric limits apply; different readings of what was revised, when it became effective, or which discharge points/parameters it covers would change which enforceable limit is selected for comparison against reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Changed WET monitoring frequency to once/quarter using Daphnia pulex and Pimephales promelas;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies WET monitoring frequency (once per quarter) and required test species; alternative interpretations of frequency counting, quarter boundaries, or species substitution would change whether monitoring was required and whether evidence satisfies the obligation.

candidates.exact_span: Cadmium, 2,3,7,8-TCDD Dioxin, Pentachlorophenol, Aldrin, Chlordane and Toxaphene pollutants monitoring requirements have been added;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Adds monitoring obligations for named pollutants; interpretation of which parameters, outfalls, frequencies, and effective dates are covered by 'added' requirements would change whether monitoring was required for each evaluated period.

candidates.exact_span: Cyanide limits and compliance schedules have been established.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes cyanide numeric limits and associated compliance schedules; different readings of schedule timing, interim vs final limits, or whether limits are enforceable during FY2025 would change applicable limit selection (A) and whether missing or delayed results reflect a documented no-data/compliance-schedule state versus required-but-unmet monitoring (C).

candidates.exact_span: The facility is required to sample and report all the priority pollutants identified in Part D, Expanded Effluent Testing Data of Form 2A.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a broad monitoring-and-reporting obligation tied to Form 2A Part D priority pollutants; interpretation of which pollutants fall in Part D, reporting frequency, and how this general requirement interacts with permit-specific limits would change evaluated monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: From that list, the pollutants in Table 1 were either tested above the minimum quantification levels (MQLs) or were tested at detection levels above EPA MQL or not meeting Sufficiently Sensitive Test Method requirements at 40 CFR 136.1(c) and reported as being non-detect.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classifies pollutants by MQL exceedance, elevated detection level, insufficiently sensitive methods, or non-detect status; different interpretations of MQL thresholds, method sensitivity under 40 CFR 136.1(c), and non-detect reporting would change whether a numeric comparison is possible (A) and how missing or below-quantification evidence is categorized (C).

candidates.exact_span: When a pollutant was tested at a detection level that was greater than the EPA MQL or not meeting Sufficiently Sensitive Test method requirements, then for screening purposes that pollutant will be assumed to have a concentration at that detection level.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Prescribes a screening assumption that assigns a numeric concentration equal to the detection level under specified conditions; alternative readings of when the assumption applies, what counts as the detection level, or whether 'screening purposes' governs compliance comparison would change exceedance determinations (A) and the evidentiary status of otherwise non-detect or method-limited results (C).

candidates.exact_span: The discharge from Outfall 001 is on that water at Latitude 36° 43' 02" North, Longitude 108° 13' 15" West.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies Outfall 001 as the operative discharge point to the San Juan River segment; if limits, monitoring requirements, or missing-evidence evaluations are outfall-specific, different interpretations of outfall identity or scope would change which requirements and measurements are matched.
